payment_validity_goals.title: Payer authorization
payment_validity_goals.predicate: The payment should be authorized by the intended payer or delegate.
limits: Delegate policy and intended payer must be defined before implementation checking.

payment_validity_goals.title: Payment binding
payment_validity_goals.predicate: The payment should match the terms advertised by the service provider.
limits: Check recipient, asset, amount, network and validity interval as applicable.
The excerpt mentions advertised services; it does not define cryptographic resource-URL binding. Do not silently strengthen the goal to require a signed URL.

payment_validity_goals.title: Replay resistance
payment_validity_goals.predicate: The same payment should not be settleable more than once.
limits: Define payment identity and authoritative settlement before checking.
Repeated requests, transaction submissions, successful responses and ledger transfers are distinct observations.
Request idempotency and ledger replay resistance must not be conflated.

reconstructed_server_oriented_claim.text: A released resource should correspond to an authorized, correctly parameterized, and non-reused payment.
reconstructed_server_oriented_claim.operational_expectation_as_supplied: A service provider releases a resource only after verification or settlement.
limits: Verification and settlement are distinct events.
The table below demands settlement before delivery, which is stronger than verification alone.
The table formulas do not separately state payer authorization or the replay-resistance property; these require their own formalization or model invariants.

documented_mechanisms_as_described_by_us.mechanism: signed payment payload checked against advertised requirements
exact EVM checks payer authorization, recipient, asset, amount, validity interval and chain-specific settlement state
payment identifier for idempotent retries and duplicate-settlement handling

intended_restrictions: should not receive authority to redirect payment

documentation_gaps_claimed_by_user: No comparable explicit security condition for a malicious service provider.
No precise treatment of malicious or faulty facilitator behavior beyond high-level trust minimization.
threat_model.principle: No operator or payment delegatee is inherently trustworthy; each stakeholder must be explicitly covered by the threat model.
capabilities_not_fully_specified: corruption timing and key compromise semantics

formalization_notes: Formulas preserve supplied event names, quantification, shared variables and strict temporal ordering; no setup-before-action constraint was added.
Client receipt uses existential tx2, not necessarily the settled tx, exactly as supplied.
Honest and malicious labels are scenario names; their operational semantics require the missing model.
No Tamarin model, lemma execution log, proof object or counterexample trace accompanies this excerpt.
Ev_PaymentSettled must represent authoritative ledger settlement, not merely facilitator success reporting.
Ev_ServerDelivered and Ev_ClientReceived require explicit mappings to protected resource delivery; handler execution or external side effects are not automatically equivalent.

motivating_incident_claims.claim: A reportedly leaked administrator key enabled ownership takeover and draining USDC from wallets that had granted allowances.
motivating_incident_claims.classification_in_excerpt: deployment key-management failure, not established protocol flaw

motivating_incident_claims.claim: A subsequent audit of over 30 x402 projects reportedly found excessive owner privileges widespread.
Earlier payment-platform hot wallet compromises motivate explicit operator trust analysis.

overall_assessment_as_supplied.text: The excerpt argues that x402 implicitly targets payment validity but does not fully account for payment-service exchange and party trust assumptions; secure deployment therefore requires deployment-specific safeguards.
